rationale.all: Retain the existing AI literacy and AI social-engineering teaching, then apply it through bank cases, platform architecture and threat checks. A 4h Foundation course budget preserves substantive threat awareness; the internal showcase uses 90 minutes and requires verified bank examples.
rationale.entry: Build with Andrew provides accessible, no-code prompting and iteration. Its app project is an L1 practice example; it does not demonstrate agent-builder competence. The bank lab teaches work context, checking and accountable use.
rationale.practitioner: Evaluating AI Agents supplies tracing and evaluation practice; Agent Skills adds reusable instructions and tool use; inherited safe-use knowledge and agent-security guidance support supervision. Internal exercises supply ownership, recovery and domain-specific sign-off. Python readiness is required for the evaluation course; validate Skills exercises in the pilot.
rationale.technical: A coherent multi-agent programme develops build and deployment skills; Reasoning with o1 adds routing and cost/latency decisions; Improving Accuracy adds known-answer evaluation. This pathway is for code-ready builders. Pilot all notebooks, especially o1-era examples, before assigning; the coached adaptation serves no-code builders. Security architecture and infrastructure remain separately assigned roles.
rationale.governance: Governance fundamentals and an autonomy framework support a bank-specific risk case; governance responsibility does not require L3.
rationale.grc-builder: The same governance role content is layered over L3 only for people who also build agents.
rationale.leadership: A short autonomy framework supports decision vocabulary. The bank studio and quarterly forums teach workflow change, accountability and vendor decisions using bank evidence.
rationale.cdc: Inherited agent-security teaching is supplemented by a timed bank incident drill. A separate introductory course would repeat inherited content.
rationale.forensics: Careful Adoption adds protected logging and recovery guidance; a trace-preservation and reconstruction exercise supplies practical evidence.
rationale.threat-intelligence: Agent threat research supports N5.7 threat-landscape responsibility, with bank-specific monitoring and detection updates.
rationale.idp: Assign the governance branch to staff who assess AI/data risk. DLP-only staff should retain relevant supervision outcomes and remove governance responsibilities they do not hold.
rationale.biso: Governance fundamentals and the agent-security matrix support risk review and assurance; the combined branch needs a provisional 5h course budget.
rationale.testing: Agent testing guidance and an internal contained test exercise cover tester responsibilities at L2.
rationale.redteam: Advanced agent red-team teaching supports adversarial tool and protocol tests. The role can operate at L2; advanced security expertise does not imply building agents.
rationale.exposure: Exposure fundamentals and agentic risk guidance support inventory, reachability and remediation practice.
rationale.harness: AI Code Review is a direct repository-review and triage course for harness builders. Known-vulnerability benchmarks, exploit reproduction, patched/unpatched tests and reliability measures still need an internal engineering exercise.
rationale.architecture: AI security fundamentals and the agent-security matrix are assigned only to security architects. The combined branch needs a provisional 4.25h course budget.
rationale.engineering: MCP: Build Rich-Context AI Apps teaches client/server integration. Production identity, runtime isolation and deployment controls require bank implementation practice; the provider authentication roadmap is not implemented security training.
rationale.security: AI security fundamentals support security design and remediation responsibilities without requiring an agent-builder profile.
rationale.transformation: Use a bank workflow studio with baseline measures, revised work, accountability and adoption evidence. No generic organisational-redesign course is mandatory.
rationale.iam: Identity and adoption guidance support identity-operations responsibilities. The IAM drill tests grants, reviews and revocation using bank controls.
rationale.iam-integration: Identity guidance plus workload-identity implementation supports integration specialists. Their agentic level reflects how they work, not their IAM seniority.
rationale.cio: Use the leadership studio and quarterly evidence forums for strategy, vendor selection and adoption decisions. Shared course and module IDs prevent repeat assignments.

assumptions: 2027 planning proposal, version 2, based on capability model 2 and catalogue v10 assessed on 18 October 2026. Foundation is shared knowledge; L1-L3 describe work with AI, while role responsibilities and approved product access are independent. Full-course durations are counted; ranges use their upper bound. The shared course budgets are 4h Foundation, 2h L1, 8h L2 and 24h L3. Foundation uses 4h to retain the existing threat-awareness teaching. Role course budgets are provisionally 4h; architecture is 4.25h and BISO 5h. Internal learner hours are additional and proposed; they earn no syllabus-score credit. Headcounts, licences, platform approval, coach capacity and learner prerequisites require owner validation. No operational authorisation or competence is implied by coverage. Global scope excludes TR-125/TR-128/TR-129; TR-159 is excluded until its lab bundle is scoped. Existing duration overrides are retained for comparable full-resource estimates; TR-118 is a 6h reading-bundle estimate and TR-155 a 9h26m path. No source scores or assessment evidence are changed.
